question: Why did FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs adsorb more 2-CEES than pristine CNTs between 30 min and 30 h?
expect: premise false: in that period its apparent capacity stayed LOWER than pristine CNTs', attributed to concurrent catalytic degradation; it ends higher only at 48 h (636 mg/g) (sec. 3.2)
rendered:
Document "3D network carbon nanotube film supported FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy nanoparticles for integrated adsorption and detoxification of sulfur mustard simulant" answers this question.

Pristine CNTs primarily relied on physical adsorption mechanisms, including p–p interactions and van der Waals forces. In contrast, FeCoNiCrMn nanoparticles introduced multimetallic active sites that catalyzed the chemical transformation of 2-CEES, leading to partial degradation during the adsorption process. As a result, part of the adsorbed 2-CEES may have undergone catalytic conversion rather than simple accumulation, thereby reducing the net gravimetrically measured mass gain during this period.
